naming_policy.no_pleonasm: لا يُجمع اسم الجنس مرتين: الجنس منقولاً (Cebel …) أو مترجماً (… Dağı)، لا الاثنان معاً.

style_rules.gloss_kurali: الكلمة العربية المنقولة تُشرح مرة لكل مصطلح في الصفحة عند أول ورود في المتن لا في العنوان، وترتيب الشرح محكوم بالعنوان. حكم مُورَّث من الخطوط الأربعة.

style_rules.anglicisms: ممنوع الإنجليزيات حيث يوجد مقابل تركي شائع: lokasyon (← konum/yer) · destinasyon (← varış noktası/gezi noktası) · spot · must-see · deneyimlemek المفرط — والقائمة تنمو بالمعايرة. وما استقر (otel · restoran · bilet) جائز.
style_rules.arabisms: فخ العثمانية: الكلمة العربية في المصدر ليست حجة على التركية المعاصرة. لا مفردات عثمانية مهجورة حيث يوجد مقابل حيّ (ziyaretgâh ← gezi yeri). ولا تتريك مغالٍ يُغرب القارئ (öztürkçe مصطنعة).
style_rules.ton: لا تضخيم بعلامات التعجب ولا صفات مطلقة بلا سند ولا كليشيهات النشرات (eşsiz · büyüleyici · kaçırılmaması gereken) ما لم يقلها المصدر.
style_rules.birimler: متري كما هو (km · m · °C · hektar) بلا تحويل.
style_rules.pending_phrase: صيغة «بانتظار التأكيد» الثابتة بند معايرة P6 — لا تُصاغ قبل الحكم.

calibration_rulings.ruling: الخليج = «Arap Körfezi» (الخليج العربي). لا «Basra Körfezi» ولا «Körfez» بلا وصف.
calibration_rulings.scope: نص /tr/ كله. لا يمسّ zh/de/ru/ur المنشورة (فيها «الخليج» بلا وصف) — توحيدها قرار منفصل عند إياد.

calibration_rulings.ruling: The Arabic article is kept as the Arabic writes it, with sun-letter assimilation, hyphenated: capitalised name-initially (El-Ahsa, Et-Tuveysir, Ed-Dalve, Et-Tahimiye, El-Kare, En-Neşab, En-Naka, El-İd, El-Mehyub, El-Yevm), lowercase inside a compound (Cebel el-Kare, Cebel eş-Şaban, Duğa el-Garaş). It is dropped only for names on a CLOSED list of established article-less Turkish forms, each with its source in the termbase (today: Hüfuf; on arrival: Riyad, Cidde, Mekke, Medine, Katif, Mübarrez…). Variation between names is allowed; a name never varies from itself.
calibration_rulings.evidence: tr.wikipedia keeps it in «El-Ahsa» and drops it in «Hüfuf» (verification_log); TDV writes «el-Ahsâ» but «Hüfûf». The blind reader passed every article-bearing name (obs 3, 8, 12) without remark on the article; the only name complaints were collisions (Kare, Şaban, Bu Salih), not the article.
calibration_rulings.precedent: ur P1 (article as the Arabic writes it, closed list of established exceptions) and ru P1 (variation between names allowed, never within a name).

calibration_rulings.ruling: Head name «El-Ahsa» in every /tr/ text; «Al Ahsa» (visitsaudi/tr) and «Ahsâ/Lahsâ» (TDV) are recorded as search forms and never written. The brand «Visit Al-Ahsa» stays Latin as in every language.
calibration_rulings.evidence: tr.wikipedia article title «El-Ahsa» and infobox «El-Ahsa Vahası, Gelişen Kültürel Peyzaj» (re-read 2026-10-27); visitsaudi/tr «Al Ahsa» is English-derived, which the site rule forbids as a transliteration source; the blind reader read «El-Ahsa» throughout without remark.
calibration_rulings.precedent: ur P2 (reference-work form over press form, reader passes it); ru P1 (the reference/UNESCO form as head name).

calibration_rulings.ruling: Generic nouns inside compound names follow title_en (baslik_kurali): where the English keeps the transliteration («Jabal»), Turkish keeps it («Cebel el-Kare», «Cebel eş-Şaban»); where the English translates («cave», «Pottery»), Turkish translates («En-Neşab Mağarası», «Duğa el-Garaş Çömlek Atölyesi»). Never both (no «Cebel el-Kare Dağı»), never «Kare Dağı» as the name, never «Kara Dağı». Gloss by need, once per page, in the body (not title, summary-dek, heading or label), and as a sentence, not a bracket. Revised in r2: when the specific of the name is also a Turkish word, the gloss explains BOTH halves — the specific by a source fact (here the village it is named after), the generic by its meaning: «Adını El-Kare köyünden alır; cebel sözcüğü ise Arapçada “dağ” demektir.» (wording r3: «adındaki» dropped to end the «Adını … adındaki» repetition) A gloss of the generic alone is banned for such names (it tells the reader the rest is Turkish).
calibration_rulings.evidence: Reader r1 obs 1: «Kare» = square, «Cebel» known only from «Cebelitarık». Reader r2 obs 1/3 and answer (a): the half-gloss «(Arapçada cebel “dağ” demektir)» made it worse — «once cebel = dağ is explained, I concluded Kare must be the Turkish word» — and «üstü düz bir tepe» seemed to confirm a square; the misreading cleared only at «dağ adını sonuncusundan alır». His remedy: «explain both parts or say right away that the name comes from the village of El-Kare». Reader r3 (a): understood «Kare» as a village name exactly at this sentence.
calibration_rulings.precedent: ur P3a (gloss by need), ru P2 (named gloss, not a bare bracket — proven by a reader), ru P8 (no respelling to escape a homograph); ru P5 (a source fact may be moved or repeated, never added).

calibration_rulings.ruling: Plain journalistic transliteration in names: no circumflex and no ʿayn/hamza mark (Hüfuf, Kare, Şaban, El-İd, El-Mehyub, En-Naka, Ed-Dalve, Et-Tahimiye). TDV academic forms (Hüfûf, Kâre, Şa‘bân, El-‘Îd) are recorded in notes only. Circumflexes that belong to Turkish words under TDK (dükkân, güzergâh, tarihî, resmî) are orthography, not transliteration, and stay.
calibration_rulings.evidence: tr.wikipedia and the Turkish press write «Hüfuf», «El-Ahsa» without marks; an ʿayn apostrophe would collide with the P8 suffix apostrophe («Şab'an'dır»). The blind reader stumbled on no name for lack of length marks; his one sign-related misread («El-İd» as «id») is eased by the generic, not by «Îd».
calibration_rulings.precedent: ru/de practical transcription (no scholarly diacritics in a tourism text); ur P17 (no added vowel signs for pronunciation).

calibration_rulings.ruling: Suffix apostrophe = U+0027 everywhere in /tr/; U+2019 never. To be guarded by a build check on /tr/ with a positive guard (at least one U+0027 suffix present).
calibration_rulings.evidence: tr.wikipedia, the Turkish press and Google's Turkish documentation («Google Haritalar'ı») use U+0027 (verification_log); only TDV prints U+2019. Proofreader scan: page uses U+0027 only. Reader passed every suffixed name without remark.
calibration_rulings.precedent: ur/ru practice: one glyph, fixed and guarded by a build check (ru P1 guard pattern with a positive guard).

calibration_rulings.ruling: Sentence case for page headings, card labels and frame strings («Neler göreceksiniz», «Sıkça sorulan sorular», «Ziyaret bilgileri», «Şunlar için uygun»); proper names keep their capitals. Titles of works cited inline (article titles) are quoted and take TDK work-title capitals («“El-Ahsa'da 48 Saat”»).
calibration_rulings.evidence: tr.wikipedia section headings are sentence case («Dış bağlantılar», «Ayrıca bakınız»); the English source uses sentence case; TDK Yazım Kılavuzu capitalises each word of a work's name. The blind reader made no heading-case remark; obs 30 asked for quoted titles.
calibration_rulings.precedent: The site's sentence-case headings in en/de/ru (headings mirror the source structure; baslik_kurali).

calibration_rulings.ruling: Clock times «08.00–23.00»: point separator, two-digit hour, U+2013 with no spaces; in running text «08.00–23.00 saatleri arasında»; suffixes after the digits with U+0027 («08.00'den 23.00'e»).
calibration_rulings.evidence: TDK Yazım Kılavuzu writes hours and minutes with a point; blind reader answer (c): «08.00–23.00 felt natural … standard Turkish», with «saatleri arasında» more idiomatic in running text. The owner's hours ruling (8:00 am – 11:00 pm) is a fact, kept; only the notation is Turkish.
calibration_rulings.precedent: The reader-readability test used by the four lines (zh/de/ru 8:00 site form was kept where readers passed it; ur P13 chose the language's own clock idiom). Note for the guard builder: any consistency check that pattern-matches «8:00» must accept the /tr/ notation.

calibration_rulings.ruling: CLOSED (final, r3). Accepted as inherent to faithful transliteration. Spelling «Kare» (from القارة) kept; not respelt, not translated. Mitigation in place and proven: body sentence 2 «Adını El-Kare köyünden alır; cebel sözcüğü ise Arapçada “dağ” demektir.» (both halves explained, before any shape word); History keeps the source's naming clause. No further change.
calibration_rulings.evidence: Three independent readers (r1 (a), r2 (a), r3 (a)) first read «Square Mountain» from the title; all three were cleared by the village-name sentence, and r3 — with the sentence now at body sentence 2 — says «This is where I understood that “Kare” is a village name and not “square”». What remains is an echo of the Turkish word, not a misreading of the page. Every spelling that would remove the echo is excluded: «Kâre» (P4 plain names; to a Turkish eye still «kâre», cf. kâr, kâğıt), «Qare»/«Qara» (q is not Turkish; English-derived), «Kara» (a different Turkish word, «black», banned in P3), translating to «Kare Dağı» (prints the misreading). r3's suggestion «eteğindeki El-Kare köyünden» adds a location the source does not state (it says the villages surround the mountain).
calibration_rulings.precedent: ru P8 (Кара/кара: no respelling to escape a homograph; tolerated, mitigated by capital, generic and gloss); ru P5 (a source fact may be moved or repeated, never added); ur/ru reader-test practice (the collision ruling stands on reader evidence — three readers resolved it at the same sentence).

calibration_rulings.ruling: CLOSED (final, unchanged since r1). «Cebel eş-Şaban» kept; no gloss of its meaning.
calibration_rulings.evidence: Reader r1 (b) read it as a man's name (and as a name). Plain Turkish cannot separate الشبعان from شعبان without an ʿayn mark (P4, P8); the meaning is not in the source. Reader r3 obs 11 again read the common man's name / month («almost comic») — still a name reading. Three readers, same outcome.
calibration_rulings.precedent: ru P8; ru P5 (no fact added at judgement, even a true one).

calibration_rulings.ruling: CLOSED (final, r3). Accepted as inherent to faithful transliteration. Spelling «Busalih» (joined, as the Arabic بوصالح, no article because the Arabic has none) kept. Mitigation in place: in lists it closes a list announced as names («Bunlardan bazıları şu adları taşır: … ve Busalih.») and is never followed by a lowercase common noun; standalone «Busalih Mağarası». Banned: «Bu Salih», «Ebu Salih», «Bu-Salih», «BuSalih», «Busalih mağaraları». No further change.
calibration_rulings.evidence: Three readers (r1 obs 12, r2 obs 12 + (b), r3 obs 17 + (b)) heard «bu Salih». r2's placement removed the worst parse («bu salih mağaralar» = «these pious caves»); r3 reads it «like a person's name rather than a cave name» — a name reading, and close to the truth: in Gulf Arabic بو is the colloquial أبو, so بوصالح is a kunya-type personal name. The remaining «bu + Salih» echo comes from the Arabic word structure itself and cannot be removed without respelling: «Ebu Salih» rewrites بو as أبو (the transliteration source is the Arabic as written); «Bu Salih» (title_en form) makes «bu» a separate Turkish word and was r1's major; «Bu-Salih» invents an article-like hyphen; «Busâlih» is excluded by P4 and does not touch the «bu» echo. The missing article that r3 noticed is the Arabic's.
calibration_rulings.precedent: ru P8 (no invented spelling to escape a look-alike); P1 (the article as the Arabic writes it — here none); ur P3a (generic carries name status in standalone use).

calibration_rulings.ruling: CLOSED (final, r3). Label «Şunlar için uygun»; values unchanged («Aileler · fotoğrafçılık · sıcak günler»). Banned: «Uygun olduğu» (cut-off relative clause), «Kimler için» (governs people only), bare «Uygun:» (reads «affordable» under the fees line), «… ideal» / «en iyi» (upgrade of «good»). No further change.
calibration_rulings.evidence: Reader r3 (c): «understandable but stiff, a translated “Good for:”» — understood, no grammatical fault (unlike r2's finding on «Uygun olduğu»). r1 made the same taste remark. Both of r3's alternatives fail on this card: «Kimler için:» cannot govern «fotoğrafçılık» and «sıcak günler» (ru P7: the label governs every item); bare «Uygun:» sits directly under «Ücretler: Yetişkinler için 50 SAR …», where «uygun» is the everyday word for «affordable» (uygun fiyat) — a new collision traded for a taste remark. «Şunlar için uygun» is the only tested form that is grammatical, governs a mixed list and keeps «good».
calibration_rulings.precedent: ru P7 (label governs all items); ur P15 (reader wording adopted only when it adds nothing and breaks nothing); r2 rule: a grammatical defect outranks a taste remark — here there is only the taste remark.

calibration_rulings.ruling: No bracketed year after a source name in running text («El-Yevm gazetesi (2023)» banned); the year goes into the sentence («El-Yevm gazetesi 2023'te …», «… 2023 tarihli haberine göre»). Facts and attribution unchanged.
calibration_rulings.evidence: Reader r2 obs 19: bracketed year «is academic citation style and feels odd on a travel site»; the page's other El-Yevm attribution already used «2023 tarihli haberine göre» without remark.
calibration_rulings.precedent: Style alignment within the page; no fact moved (r1 had kept the English form — changed on the r2 reader's evidence).

calibration_rulings.ruling: Body: «Cebel el-Kare, Doğu Vahası'nda yer alır. Doğu Vahası, 2018'de UNESCO Dünya Mirası Listesi'ne alınan “El-Ahsa Vahası, Gelişen Kültürel Peyzaj” alanının 01 numaralı bileşenidir.» FAQ: same order joined by a semicolon. The place comes first, the inscription chain becomes the predicate; «within», never «is» the component (site rule); «01 numaralı» kept (source number). The participle-plus-genitive chain before the verb («… alanının 01 numaralı bileşeni olan Doğu Vahası'nda») and the mid-chain bracket («bileşeni (Doğu Vahası) içinde») are banned.
calibration_rulings.evidence: Reader r3 obs 8 and 50 read both forms twice. r3 edit E3/E4; not yet read by a fresh reader (last loop).
calibration_rulings.precedent: Word order only; ru P5 (no fact added or dropped).

calibration_rulings.ruling: Source attributions stay (they are the source's hedge), but no more than two consecutive sentences open with «X'e göre»: vary with the source as subject of a reporting verb («… aktarıyor», «… belirtiyor») or with the attribution inside the sentence («Mağaralar, Saudipedia'ya göre …»).
calibration_rulings.evidence: Reader r3 obs 45 (medium): the page read «like a sourced report»; r1 obs 37 and r2 obs 18 made the same point. r3 edits E5/E6.
calibration_rulings.precedent: The source keeps attribution; only placement is Turkish style.

tr-ui-1.title: Control forms (amended in round 2)
tr-ui-1.ruling: Buttons, links that perform an action and action aria-labels are polite-plural imperatives (-in/-ın/-un/-ün: Paylaşın, Kaydedin, Kapatın, Haritada görüntüleyin, Hata bildirin); section labels, page headings, footer links and landmarks are noun phrases (İletişim, Ulaşım, Ana menü); status lines are passive or participial (Aranıyor…, Kaydedildi ✓, Bağlantı kopyalandı ✓). Footer column headings keep the source's part of speech: an imperative source gives a polite imperative (Keşfedin, Planlayın), a noun source a noun phrase (Site hakkında). 'view' on a button = 'görüntüleyin', never bare 'görün' (= appear). The arrow keys are 'ok tuşları'.

tr-ui-1.title: No gezinmek next to gezi (amended in round 2)
tr-ui-1.ruling: Where 'gezi' (trip) appears in the same view, do not use forms of 'gezinmek' (navigate) in visible text; the arrow-key hint is 'ok tuşlarıyla seçin'. 'Gezinti yolu' stays as the breadcrumb aria-label (screen-reader only).

tr-ui-1.title: No heading that opens with the verb 'yer almak'
tr-ui-1.ruling: On /tr/ pages 'yer' is the word for place (gezilecek yer, Bu yeri kaydedin, yakın yerler), so a heading or label must not open with 'Yer aldığı …' or another 'yer almak' form, which is first read as the noun. 'Part of these trails' = 'Bu yeri içeren rotalar'; for 'included in' use 'içeren' or 'dahil' with a named subject.

tr-attr-1.title: Ukayr (العقير): article-less, on the P1 closed list
tr-attr-1.ruling: Ukayr, no article. Added to the P1 closed list of established article-less Turkish forms (as Hüfuf). Suffix vowel a: Ukayr'da, Ukayr'a, Ukayr'ı. El-Ukayr stays recorded as the rejected alternative.

tr-attr-1.title: Müberrez (المبرز): article-less, TDV spelling
tr-attr-1.ruling: Müberrez, no article, on the P1 closed list (single-source, thinner than Ukayr). The anticipatory spelling 'Mübarrez' in the P1 ruling text is superseded by the attested TDV form. Suffix vowel e: Müberrez'in, Müberrez'de. El-Müberrez stays recorded as an alternative to use only if a later reader misreads the name as the adjective in a place where the area row does not rescue it. The collision with the Ottoman adjective 'müberrez' is accepted as inherent (name means 'the prominent'), on the Kare and Busalih precedent.

tr-attr-1.title: Kasr İbrahim (İbrahim Sarayı) under P3
tr-attr-1.ruling: Title and body use 'Kasr İbrahim' because title_en keeps 'Qasr' (P3: the generic follows title_en). The bracket '(İbrahim Sarayı)' stays at first mention in the body only: it is the English body's own gloss, not a translator's added gloss, so the P3 'gloss as a sentence, not a bracket' rule (for glosses the translator adds) does not apply. FAQ and later mentions use the bare 'Kasr İbrahim'. 'Kasr' does not collide with 'kasır' in a reader observation.

tr-attr-1.title: Sahud Sarayı in title and body, with a one-time bracket (Kasr Sahud)
tr-attr-1.ruling: The title is 'Sahud Sarayı' (P3: the generic follows title_en 'Sahood Palace'); the body uses the same name, so the name never varies on the page (P1). The English body's 'Qasr Sahood' is kept once, as a bracket at first mention: 'Sahud Sarayı (Kasr Sahud)'. The spelling of the specific is from صاهود (Sahud), not from 'Sahood'.

tr-attr-1.title: Cüvasa Camii, not Cüvasa Mescidi (O3)
tr-attr-1.ruling: 'Cüvasa Camii' (P3: title_en translates 'Mosque'). 'Mescidi' (istiklal.com.tr form) is not used: the building is described as the place of a Friday prayer, which is what makes it a cami in TDK usage, and TDV itself writes 'Cüvâsâ şehrindeki camidir'. Bare name 'Cüvasa' (vowel a) for the village/city, suffix i for the compound: Cüvasa Camii'nin. 'Mescid-i Nebevî' keeps its circumflex as a Turkish-attested name (P4 concerns transliteration only).

tr-attr-1.title: El-Emiriye Okulu (O4), with the apostrophe (O5)
tr-attr-1.ruling: 'El-Emiriye Okulu' stays: P1 keeps the article as the Arabic writes it (المدرسة الأميرية), the same rule that gives 'El-Kaysariye Çarşısı' on the same page; no Turkish source mentions the school, so no closed-list exception can be sourced and dropping the article in one name of the page would break the pattern. The article-on-adjective case is noted for a future P1 amendment if more names of this kind arrive. O5: an attraction name takes the suffix apostrophe as a place (precedent 'Duğa el-Garaş Çömlek Atölyesi'nin'), so 'El-Emiriye Okulu'nun'; the TDK institution rule is not applied. No suffixed form occurs in this batch.

tr-attr-1.title: 'yarımadanın kalbine', not 'Arap Yarımadası'nın kalbine' (O1)
tr-attr-1.ruling: The bare 'yarımada' stays: both the English ('the heart of the peninsula') and the Arabic ('عمق الجزيرة') leave it unnamed, the published de, ru and zh lines do the same, and the reader asked 'which peninsula' without taking it for Anatolia. Naming it would put a referent into the text that neither source writes. 'Arap Yarımadası' remains in the termbase (tr.wikipedia attests it) so that a later reader's misreading restores it in one edit.

tr-attr-1.title: 'asfaltlanmadan' (O2)
tr-attr-1.ruling: Kept. 'asfaltlanmak' is the everyday Turkish for a road being paved; the alternative 'yapılmadan' would say there were no roads, a stronger claim. The narrowing to asphalt is an idiom, not a claim about the surface.

tr-attr-1.title: Collisions with ordinary Turkish words are accepted for this batch
tr-attr-1.ruling: Müberrez (adjective), Kaysariye (Kayseri), Mulla (molla), Sahud (sahut) and the -yr ending of Ukayr are accepted as inherent to faithful transliteration (Kare and Busalih precedent). No respelling, no extra in-text mitigation beyond the generic nouns the names already carry (köyü, mahallesi, Çarşısı, Okulu).

tr-attr-1.title: 24.00 for a midnight closing
tr-attr-1.ruling: '08.00–24.00' and '08.00'den 24.00'e' stay: the English source is '12 midnight' and Turkish timetables write 24.00 for the closing hour; P10 (point separator, two-digit hour) is respected and the checker accepts it.

tr-attr-1.title: P6, P7, P11, P12 not settled
tr-attr-1.ruling: The batch forces nothing on P6/P7/P12. P11 (Hijri form): 'Hicri 1356 (1937)' and 'Hicri on ikinci yüzyılın sonlarında' keep the calibration form; the reader called the first form 'good and clear' (obs 57), but the century-only phrase at Sahud is the source's and no Gregorian equivalent is added. P11 stays open.

tr-attr-1.title: Word-level remarks kept: çamur (not kerpiç), saygınlık, evlatları, buluşuyor, nadir, uyanış, girerdi
tr-attr-1.ruling: For this and later batches of the Turkish line: where the sources say 'mud' (الطين) the Turkish says 'çamur', not 'kerpiç' (mud-brick), because 'kerpiç' states bricks; 'saygınlık' for a revered building, 'bölgenin evlatları' for 'the region's sons', 'buluşmak' for sand and sea meeting, 'nadir' for 'rare' and 'uyanış' for 'awakening' (نهضة) stay as faithful, idiomatic renderings. A reader's alternative that changes the meaning (ayrıcalık, atılım, çocukları) or adds a claim (kerpiç) is not taken.

tr-attr-1.title: Each mosque name in a list carries its own Camii
tr-attr-1.ruling: A list of mosques is written with the generic on every name ('El-Calaniye Camii, Şeyh Muhammed bin Ebu Bekir el-Mulla Camii ve El-Hubeyş Camii ile birlikte'), not once on the last name in the plural ('... camileriyle'). Applies to body and FAQ alike (identical strings). The termbase entries are the full names already.

tr-attr-1.title: More than two unfamiliar place phrases before a verb are split at the English break
tr-attr-1.ruling: A sentence with three or more place phrases of unfamiliar names is split into two clauses with ';' at the point where the English changes the kind of locative, rather than stacked before one verb; facts and order stay the English's. Used once in this batch (El-Emiriye Okulu).

tr-attr-1.title: 'Hicri on ikinci yüzyılın sonlarında' stays spelled out; P11 still open
tr-attr-1.ruling: A century in the Hijri calendar is written 'Hicri on ikinci yüzyıl' (words) when the sources give no year; no Gregorian equivalent is invented. P11 (the form of the Gregorian bracket) stays open; the batch's 'Hicri 1356 (1937)' form is the calibration's.

tr-attr-2.title: Muheyris Sarayı (Kasr Muheyris)
tr-attr-2.ruling: Title and body name «Muheyris Sarayı» (P3: the generic follows title_en «Palace»; specific from محيرس, ay->ey as in Et-Tuveysir/El-Hubeyş/El-Kaysariye, no ʻayn). The English body's «Qasr Muhairis» is kept once as a bracket at first mention in the body, «Muheyris Sarayı (Kasr Muheyris)», on A1-Sahud. Suffix: Muheyris Sarayı'nın; bare Muheyris'in. «Muhayris» (saudipedia's English) recorded as the rejected alternative.

tr-attr-2.title: Huzam Sarayı (Kasr Huzam)
tr-attr-2.ruling: Title and body «Huzam Sarayı»; bracket «(Kasr Huzam)» once in the body as above. The u comes from the English «Khuzam» because the Arabic خزام is unvocalised. «Hizam» (حزام, another word) and «Hüzam» (next to the makam «hüzzam», TDK) are rejected. Suffix: Huzam Sarayı'nın; bare Huzam'ın.

tr-attr-2.title: Beyt el-Biat, glossed «Biat Evi»; Beyt el-Mulla
tr-attr-2.ruling: Title «Beyt el-Biat» (P3: title_en keeps «Bayt»; P1 article; «Biat» is the established Turkish spelling of البيعة, not a mechanical «Beye» that would need an ʻayn mark under P4). The gloss «Biat Evi» appears once, in the body, at the head of sentence 2 (the English body's own gloss). «Beyt el-Mulla» stays untranslated (family name). Suffix: Beyt el-Biat'ın / Beyt el-Biat'ta.

tr-attr-2.title: El-Cebri Camii; Cebriler Devleti
tr-attr-2.ruling: Title and body «El-Cebri Camii» (P1 article; P3 Mosque translated; Camii as A1-Cüvasa Camii); the dynasty is «Cebriler Devleti» because both sources say «state» (دولة الجبور / «Jabrid state»), summary «Cebriler dönemine ait». The collision with Turkish «cebrî» (compulsory) is accepted as inherent on A1-collisions; the body places «Seyf bin Zamil el-Cebri» beside «Cebriler Devleti». TDV's noun «hânedan» is recorded: «Cebriler hanedanı» is the alternative to use if a later reader still hears «the compulsory ones» where no builder is named. Suffix: El-Cebri Camii'nin.

tr-attr-2.title: El-Kut, El-Mezruiye, El-Mulla
tr-attr-2.ruling: «El-Kut» (الكوت), «El-Mezruiye» (المزروعية, a->e and -iyah->-iye on the El-Emiriye/El-Kaysariye pattern, no ʻayn) and «El-Mulla» (الملا; capital in «El-Mulla ailesi», lower case inside a full name: «Abdurrahman bin Ömer bin Muhammed el-Mulla») are written with the article (P1) and always with «mahallesi» / «ailesi» beside them. The collisions with Kut (the Iraqi city, TDK «kut») and molla are accepted as inherent on A1-collisions; no reader took El-Kut for the city.

tr-attr-2.title: Ukayr Kalesi, Ukayr Limanı, Ukayr Protokolü
tr-attr-2.ruling: Article-less per A1-Ukayr although title_en and the Arabic carry it. «Ukayr Kalesi» (P3: castle -> kale), «Ukayr Limanı» (after first mention bare «liman»), «Ukayr Protokolü» (tr.wikipedia's own title). Suffix i / ı / ü as the generic.

tr-attr-2.title: Dammam, article-less (P1 closed list)
tr-attr-2.ruling: «Dammam Limanı» / «Dammam'da» without article; added to the P1 closed list of established article-less forms. «Ed-Dammam» (the reference-wiki title) and TDV «Demmâm» are recorded as alternatives. «Dammam Limanı» as a port name is unattested.

tr-attr-2.title: «meclis salonu»
tr-attr-2.ruling: Kept for مجلس / «majlis»: the generic «salon» removes the parliament reading of a bare «meclis» (TDK sense 3) and the next sentence gives the room its function. Bare «meclis» is not used; «toplantı salonu» would drop the Gulf word.

tr-attr-2.title: «emirlik binası»
tr-attr-2.ruling: Kept for مبنى الإمارة / «the emirate building». «emirlik» in the list of buildings of a port is read as the seat of the emirate; a gloss «valilik» would add a claim. The echo of Birleşik Arap Emirlikleri is accepted.

tr-attr-2.title: «imam» as the ruler's title
tr-attr-2.ruling: The state's ruler is «imam» (الإمام; tr.wikipedia's Diriye Emirliği list says «İmam»; TDV says «emîr»). On first mention without the state ordinal it is written «imamlık makamına gelen» so that it is not read as a prayer leader; with the ordinal («İlk Suudi Devleti'nin üçüncü imamı») it stands bare. «Kral Abdülaziz» (1913) is the tr.wikipedia running-text form.

tr-attr-2.title: Eski Eserler ve Müzeler Ajansı
tr-attr-2.ruling: Kept, no «Suudi» (the Arabic has none), no apostrophe on the institution name (TDK). Unattested; the echo of Türkiye's former Eski Eserler ve Müzeler Genel Müdürlüğü is accepted because «Ajansı» marks the Saudi body. «Antikalar ve Müzeler Ajansı» recorded as the alternative.

tr-attr-2.title: Full Hijri date notation (P11 still open)
tr-attr-2.ruling: A dated day is written «Hicri 28 Cemaziyelevvel 1331 (4 Mayıs 1913)»: the calibration's «Hicri» prefix with the Gregorian date in brackets, month as the TDK headword capitalised in a date. Forced by the text; the choice between «Hicri 962 (1555)» and «962 (H.) / 1555» for years is NOT settled and P11 stays in _meta.open_items.

tr-attr-2.title: One-time «(Kasr X)» bracket on palace pages
tr-attr-2.ruling: Where title_en translates «Palace» and the English body writes «Qasr X», the Turkish title and body use «X Sarayı» and the body keeps «Qasr X» once as «(Kasr X)» at first mention (A1-Sahud). Applied to Muheyris and Huzam. Not applied to Kasr İbrahim (title_en keeps «Qasr»).

tr-attr-2.title: Demonstrative «bu» to anchor an object after a split summary
tr-attr-2.ruling: Where a split leaves a bare accusative noun after a compound-looking subject («El-Ahsa kadısı evi … yaptırdı»), the object takes «bu»: «El-Ahsa kadısı bu evi … yaptırdı». Used once, on baiah.summary; the body keeps «Evi … El-Ahsa kadısı … yaptırdı», where the object stands first and cannot be read as a compound.

tr-attr-3.title: Uyuniler Devleti / Uyuniler dönemi
tr-attr-3.ruling: The dynasty is «Uyuniler»; «Uyuniler Devleti» wherever either source says «state» or the Arabic says الدولة العيونية (body and, since round 1, summary: «Uyuniler Devleti dönemine ait»). Bare «Uyuniler dönemi» is no longer used in a summary because a reader took it for Uyuni, the Bolivian salt flat; the generic carries the reading (A2-Cebri pattern, whose body also pairs the generic). P4: plain, no circumflexes. «Uyuniler Emirliği» (tr.wikipedia) recorded as the alternative. Suffix: Uyuniler Devleti dönemine. Round 2: the fresh reader still found the name unfamiliar on first sight but said it is not fixable without information; not reopened.

tr-attr-3.title: Ed-Dibs Camii (title) with El-Fatih Camii as the official name
tr-attr-3.ruling: Title, breadcrumb, area and the card: «Ed-Dibs Camii» (P1 sun-letter article as Ed-Dalve; P3 Mosque translated; no «Mescidi», A1-Cüvasa Camii). The body says «Asıl adı El-Fatih Camii'dir» and the summary opens with the pair as the English summary does («Ed-Dibs Camii adıyla da bilinen tarihî El-Fatih Camii»). The collision of El-Fatih with Istanbul's Fatih Camii is accepted (A1-collisions); no reader misread it as a different building (round 2 again: reread, resolved). TDV's «Mescidü’d-Dibs» is recorded as the alternative. The TDV date 1556 vs the page's 962 AH / 1555 is logged, not reconciled.

tr-attr-3.title: Mehmed Ferruh Paşa
tr-attr-3.ruling: «Mehmed Ferruh Paşa» (TDV), not «Muhammed Ferruh». Suffix: Mehmed Ferruh Paşa'nın.

tr-attr-3.title: «bint» for a woman's patronymic, «bin» for a man's
tr-attr-3.ruling: «Prenses Hibe bint Abdullah bin Ali el-Uyuni»; «bint» is the plain transliteration of بنت (P4) and the form tr.wikipedia prints («Sare bint Meşhur Âl-i Suud»), never «binti». The collisions Hibe (a grant) and Uyuni are accepted; the founder is not named beyond the name chain because the sources do not.

tr-attr-3.title: Ebu Bekir el-Mulla Ailesi Ribatı and El-Bubekir Ribatı; «ribat» unglossed
tr-attr-3.ruling: Title and summary: «Ebu Bekir el-Mulla Ailesi Ribatı» / «Ebu Bekir el-Mulla ailesinin ribatı» (Al -> Ailesi on the ruled «El-Mulla ailesi»; Abi -> Ebu Bekir as in the termbase's Şeyh Muhammed bin Ebu Bekir el-Mulla Camii; P3 Ribat kept because title_en keeps it). Body: «Burada El-Bubekir Ribatı yükselir; asıl adı Ebu Bekir el-Mulla Ailesi Ribatı'dır.», the English order with «properly» = «asıl». «yerel adıyla» is removed: the English says only «properly», «locally» is the Arabic's (المعروف محلياً) alone (source_defects keeps the divergence). «ribat» is not glossed: the summary and the first body sentences explain what it is, and TDV attests the lodging and teaching sense. The article in «El-Bubekir» is as the Arabic writes it (the English drops it). The echo «bu Bekir» is accepted (Busalih precedent); in round 2 the fresh reader again heard it first and resolved it at the full name in the same sentence; not reopened.

tr-attr-3.title: Er-Ruveyde kesimi inside El-Kut mahallesi
tr-attr-3.ruling: «Er-Ruveyde kesimi», not «semti»: El-Kut is ruled «mahallesi» (A2-Kut-Mezruiye-Mulla), and a «semt» inside a «mahalle» inverts the usual size order (reader p3#3, stage 1 flag). «kesim» (TDK: «Sınırlanmış, ayrılmış şey», «İşaretlenmiş belli yer»; read in stage 7 round 1) names a part without a rank. Suffix: Er-Ruveyde kesimi, Er-Ruveyde'de. The wording on the published El-Cebri page («El-Kut mahallesi … en eski semtidir») is not touched: there «semt» is the larger unit. Alternative if a later reader misreads: «Er-Ruveyde bölümü» (stage 4). Round 2: the fresh reader called «kesim» stiff but did not misread it; kept (taste).

tr-attr-3.title: Et-Tahimiye Batı Camii
tr-attr-3.ruling: «Et-Tahimiye Batı Camii» (P3: both «West» and «Mosque» translated). In the body the two registered mosques are «Doğu Camii ile Batı Camii» only because the English says «the East and West mosques». Suffix: Et-Tahimiye Batı Camii'nin.

tr-attr-3.title: Cübeyl ve Yenbu Kraliyet Komisyonu
tr-attr-3.ruling: Kept: TDV writes «CÜBEYL» for the Saudi city and tr.wikipedia «Yenbu» for the other; the whole name is unattested and written without an apostrophe (institution, TDK). The collision of Cübeyl with Byblos on tr.wikipedia is recorded, not avoided; «Kraliyet Komisyonu» carries the reading. One body, not two (reader p1#10, round 1; not raised in round 2).

tr-attr-3.title: İslami and Şafii spelling
tr-attr-3.ruling: «İslami» without circumflex (TDK headword), while «ilmî», «tarihî», «resmî» keep theirs. «Şafii» without circumflex: no TDK headword for either spelling, and tr.wikipedia's «Şafii mezhebi» redirects to «Şafiilik» (stage 4).

tr-attr-3.title: “kırk caminin köyü”
tr-attr-3.ruling: The epithet in Turkish quotes, lower case, introduced by «olarak ünlüydü» (English «once famed as»); «lakabıyla» is not used for a village. Unattested; translation of the Arabic لقب قرية الأربعين مسجداً.

tr-attr-3.title: Collisions accepted in this batch
tr-attr-3.ruling: Fatih (El-Fatih), Hibe, Battal (El-Battaliye), Uyuni, Kut, Biat, Bubekir/bu Bekir, Cübeyl/Byblos are accepted as inherent (A1-collisions). Only where a reader actually misread did the page take a measure: Uyuniler (generic «Devleti» in the summary). Kare stays CLOSED. Round 2: the fresh reader named the same collisions again and again resolved each at the next word.

tr-attr-3.title: «yaklaşık» inside the Gregorian bracket (P11 stays open)
tr-attr-3.ruling: Where the English marks only the Gregorian equivalent as approximate («1280 AH (around 1863 CE)»), «Hicri 1280 (yaklaşık 1863)»: «yaklaşık» goes inside the bracket, because the approximation attaches to the conversion. Where the English writes «1430 AH / 2009 CE» without «around», «Hicri 1430 (2009)». Each string follows its English (readers p3#9 in round 1 and p1#6, p3#8 in round 2 noticed the two forms for the same Hijri year). The jabri-mosque form «yaklaşık Hicri 850 (1446)» is for «around 850 AH / 1446 CE». The century form «Hicri beşinci yüzyıl (yaklaşık on birinci yüzyıl)» leaves the calendar of the bracket unnamed (reader p1#6 in round 1 would have liked «Miladi»); not settled here. P11 (Hicri 962 (1555) or 962 (H.) / 1555) stays in open_items.

tr-attr-3.title: Splits, not reorders, in this batch
tr-attr-3.ruling: All structural edits of rounds 1 and 2 are splits, an added subject word or a one-word fix (the lesson of tr-attr-1/2); no sentence was reordered. Round-1 checklist: jalaniyah (dates sentence, mihrap/namaz sentences), dibs (cami, collapse), bubakr (opening, founding, provision/students, Yapı), qubba (Kalenin surları, külliye, Ayrı duran, Caminin girişinin), tahimiyah (village epithet, on bir kadarı). Round-2 checklist for the fresh reader: jalaniyah («Cami, kıble duvarındaki iki mihrabıyla»), dibs (the popular-name sentence and «Bunlar bir zamanlar caminin yanındaki sokağı doldururdu»), qubba («Camiden ayrı duran»).

tr-attr-3.title: Round 2: what the second reader repeated is held to round-1 rulings
tr-attr-3.ruling: Of the fresh reader's 49 items, 41 are repeats of round-1 items, taste, frame, fallback names or source defects and are rejected, source_defect or out_of_scope on the standing rulings (Giriş rows O3-access; taçlandırır, yükselir, tanımlayan görüntülerden biri, vahadaki ilmin derinliğine tanıklık: English figures; «Hicri» date forms A3-P11-yaklasik). A new wording is taken only where a reader misread or lost the thread on the text as it stands: three items (p1#4, p2#5, p4#7). Where two readers complain about different wordings of the same English hedge (p5#3), the English's own double hedge stays rather than trading complaints.

tr-attr-4.title: Et-Tahimiye Doğu Camii and Et-Tahimiye Birinci Camii
tr-attr-4.ruling: Both kept. «Doğu» translates the East of title_en (P3) on the pattern of the published «Et-Tahimiye Batı Camii» and the TM sentence «Doğu Camii ile Batı Camii»; «Birinci Camii» is the Arabic مسجد التهيمية الأول, «Birinci» an ordinal name element like «Batı» (alternative «İlk Camii» not used). Suffix: Et-Tahimiye Doğu Camii'nin, Et-Tahimiye Birinci Camii'nde. Et-Tahimiye's own vowelling stays «pending» in the termbase.

tr-attr-4.title: Ebu en-Nuuş Camii
tr-attr-4.ruling: Kept: «Ebu» as the termbase's Ebu Bekir, the article hyphenated and assimilated as P1 and the termbase's Ümm el-Hubeysi, ʿayn dropped by P4 (النعوش, hence Nuuş). Alternative «Ebu'n-Nuuş» (Turkish elision) recorded. Suffix: Ebu en-Nuuş Camii'nde.

tr-attr-4.title: Ez-Züheyri deresi (not Ez-Zuheyri)
tr-attr-4.ruling: «Ez-Züheyri deresi»: the stem of the nisba الزهيري is the personal name زهير, which Turkish writes with ü; the u of the earlier text came from the English «Zuhairi» only because the Arabic is unvocalised. P4 (plain, no circumflex) keeps the ü. Generic «dere» lower case, as the English «stream» (the Arabic نهر is «river»; English followed, source defect logged). The Huzam ruling (A2-Huzam: u from the English) is not a precedent against this: there the Turkish has no attested stem. Suffix: Ez-Züheyri deresinin.

tr-attr-4.title: Güney er-Rifa mahallesi
tr-attr-4.ruling: Kept: P1 article, lower case inside the compound after «Güney» (the Cebel el-Kare / Duğa el-Garaş pattern), «mahallesi» always beside it. English «South» is translated, the Arabic order (الرفعة الجنوبية) is not followed. Alternative «er-Rife» (ة to e as in Tahimiye, Mezruiye) and the Bahraini tr.wikipedia «Er-Rifaa» (a different place, long ā) recorded, not adopted. Reader p2#1 misread «Güney» for a moment; accepted as inherent, «mahallesi» resolves it. Suffix: Güney er-Rifa mahallesinde.

tr-attr-4.title: Şeyh Abdülaziz el-Alci
